We apply the distributive law 

$$
AB+AC=A(B+C).
$$

So, we calculate $B+C$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}B+C & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -3 & 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}AB+AC & =A(B+C) \\  & =A{I}_{3} \\  & =A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
